newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force officer charged with sex harassment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force officer charged with sex harassment.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force colonel faces possible court martial after being charged with sexual harassment, fraternisation and conduct unbecoming of an officer, military officials said Thursday.

Col. David Rauhecker with the Air Force Special Operations Command headquartered at Hurlburt Field in the Florida Panhandle could face up to 13 years in prison for six offences including adultery, making suggestive remarks, touching a female officer in a sexual manner and having a relationship with an enlisted woman.
An investigation is continuing after a complaint was filed by a female officer involved in one of the incidents, officials said. The charges were presented Nov. 4.

Rauhecker is the eighth person and the highest ranking officer to face sexual harassment charges at Hurlburt in the past two years, Air Force spokeswoman Shirley Sikes said. He was relieved of command of the 16th Logistics Group and reassigned pending the outcome of the investigation.
Harmon Massey, Rauhecker's attorney and a retired military trial judge, said a formal hearing known as an Article 32 hearing was scheduled for Dec. 9. Massey declined to comment on the charges.

At the hearing, evidence will be brought before a board of officers, which can recommend no disciplinary action, a demotion or a general court martial. The panel will submit its recommendation to Maj. Gen. James Hobson, head of Air Force Special Operations, who will make the final decision.
Rauhecker's case comes as U.S. military branches continue to reel from a growing list of sexual harassment charges at bases around the United States.
"While the Air Force does not tolerate any form of sexual harassment, this person has not been proven to be guilty yet," Sikes said. "That is important to remember."
